title: Bishop Shanahan field hockey reaches the state semifinals
summary: The Eagles beat Gwynedd Mercy 2-1 Saturday in a PIAA Class 2A quarterfinal, with third- and fourth-quarter goals from Libby Leith and Silvana Riccardo and 10 saves from goalie Aly Civera. Shanahan, 17-6-1, plays defending state champion Palmyra on Tuesday.

title: Downingtown East edges Coatesville to stay unbeaten in district football
summary: The top-seeded Cougars won their District 1 6A quarterfinal 30-27 Friday as junior Juelz Chiron-Robinson ran for 256 yards, including touchdowns of 74 and 77 yards. East, 11-0, hosts Spring-Ford in the semifinals in what is coach Mike Matta's final season.

title: Great Valley football stays unbeaten and reaches its first 5A district semifinal
summary: The third-seeded Patriots held off Unionville 20-17 Friday night, sealed by a Cooper Callahan interception with six seconds left, to move to 12-0. It is the school's first trip to the District 1 5A semifinals; they play at Springfield (Delco) on Friday, Nov. 20, at 7 p.m.

title: Goshen Fire Company's $8.5 million station rebuild nears federal funding step
summary: Chester County plans to request release of $850,000 in federal money around Nov. 17 for rebuilding Station 54, a 1951 firehouse that would grow by nearly 39 percent with a new two-story building. Comments on the environmental review are due Nov. 16, and construction is expected to start in January 2027 and wrap up by May 2028.

title: County wants residents' input on its climate plan at a Nov. 19 open house
summary: The Chester County Planning Commission is updating the countywide Climate Action Plan and will hold a public meeting from 6 to 8 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 19, with open-house sessions around a 6:45 p.m. presentation that can also be watched on Zoom. Online comments open the same day.
loc: Government Services Center, 601 Westtown Road, West Goshen

title: Ten West Chester Area seniors named National Merit semifinalists
summary: Seven students from Henderson, two from Rustin and one from East earned the distinction, which goes to roughly the top one percent of high school seniors in each state. Separately, Peirce Middle School teacher Michael Dumas received the state's middle school Technology and Engineering Teacher Excellence Award.

title: Patrick O'Donnell, former county commissioner and longtime borough lawyer, dies at 78
summary: O'Donnell, who died Nov. 11, won a Chester County commissioner's seat in 1979 as one of the county's few elected Democrats and practiced law in West Chester for 50 years, much of it in land use and municipal work. He also spent about 25 years on the board of Good Fellowship Ambulance.

title: Six holiday weekends start Nov. 27 with store discounts and free street parking
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce expects about 40,000 visitors for its downtown holiday campaign, which opens Black Friday with many of the roughly 180 shops and restaurants offering 20 to 30 percent off and other promotions. On-street parking is free Nov. 27 through 29, and the program runs through New Year's Day.

title: Golden Valley Farms Coffee marks 40 years with a Coffee Fest on Nov. 28
summary: The family-run West Goshen roaster, which has sold certified organic coffee since 2010, celebrates on Small Business Saturday at the Artisan Exchange with free mini cold brews and hot chocolate, local vendors and tours of the roasting room.
loc: Artisan Exchange, 208 Carter Drive, West Goshen

title: Greek-style coffee shop opens on West Gay Street; 7 Brew drive-thru follows Monday
summary: Brewing Love has opened at 145 W. Gay St., pouring freddos, the iced coffee popular in Greece, along with iced matcha and pastries. Drive-thru chain 7 Brew is set to open at 829 Paoli Pike on Monday, Nov. 16.
